summary: Sicheng Liang was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Beijing Huiwen Middle School, Tsinghua University (~1915–1923), and the University of Pennsylvania School of Design (~1924–1927), later holding a post at Peking University (~1931–1937).
Sidney Lee worked in history and archaeology. He was educated at the City of London School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1878–1882), and held a post at Queen Mary University of London (~1913–1924).

Siegfried Goldschmidt studied Indology and linguistics under Albrecht Weber (1864) and Rudolf von Roth (~1867–1869) across Leipzig, Berlin, Göttingen, and Tübingen (Ph.D. 1867). He later served as an assistant professor at the University of Strasbourg in 1881.

Indologist Siegfried Lienhard studied at Vienna (Dr. phil. 1949), Paris, and Stockholm (Habilitation ~1966). He held posts at Göttingen, Banaras Hindu University, Kiel University (professor 1962–1968), and Stockholm University (professor 1968–1990), and was General Secretary of the IASS (~1972–1984).

Sieglinde Dietz is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who completed her PhD at the University of Bonn under Michael Hahn by 1980. She held a post at the University of Göttingen, attested in 1990.
Signe Cohen specializes in Indology and religious studies. A former student of Ludo Rocher, she serves as a professor at the University of Missouri.
Signe Howell studied at SOAS University of London (~1973–1975) and the University of Oxford (~1975–1980). In 1989, she held a post as professor at the University of Oslo.

Silvia Luraghi is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Turin (~1976–1980). She held posts at the University of Turin (~1988–1993), Università degli Studi Roma Tre (~1993–1999), and the University of Pavia (~1999).

Silvio Vita studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton University. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, he held posts at "L'Orientale", the Italian School of East Asian Studies, Sapienza University, and University of Naples Federico II.

Simo Knuuttila worked in philosophy and religious studies, completing studies at the University of Helsinki in 1976. He held academic posts there from ~1976 to 2014, including as professor from ~1981, and was affiliated with the Academy of Finland (1994–2004).

Simo Parpola is a linguist and historian who completed his PhD at the University of Helsinki (1961–1968). He held positions at Heidelberg, the University of Chicago (1977–1979), and the University of Helsinki (Docent 1973–1976; Professor 1978).

Simon P. James is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Durham University as a tutor in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and as a lecturer in philosophy (attested 2013–2014).
Simon Winant is an Indology and linguistics scholar. As of 2026, he is attested as both a PhD student and a faculty member at Ghent University.
Siniruddha Dash is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Director at the University of Madras (2000–2014) and as Director at the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation in 2020.

Siran Upendra Deraniyagala was an archaeologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, the University of London, and Harvard University, learning under Frank Raymond Allchin. He served as Director General of Sri Lanka's Department of Archaeology (~1992–2001).

Sisir Roy is a scholar in philosophy and other fields who studied under Debabrata SenSharma. He held posts as a professor at the Indian Statistical Institute and at the National Institute of Advanced Studies (attested 2009).
Siu-tong Kwan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong, studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and teacher Zhihua Yao.
Siyong Liang was a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. He completed his studies at Tsinghua University and Harvard University (~1924–1930).
Smita Halder is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. In 2026, she is attested as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society and studying under doctoral supervisor Susmita Basu Majumdar.

So Takahashi studied Indology and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo, earning an M.A. He held posts at Meijo University as an associate professor (attested 1977–1978) and professor (attested 1991).
